about: Classification of every hunk of a cited file in the diff of the HGQ2 snapshot (new side) against installed hgq2 0.1.9 (old side). Kinds: behavioral (code present in both behaves differently), addition (snapshot-only code or names; code present in both is unchanged under its defaults), cosmetic (no runtime effect of its own: a comment, or an import used only by another hunk). in_study: whether STUDY v0.8 section 7.3 or chang review v0.3 C16-C18 names the difference. Hunk ids are content hashes from cbl/refdiff.py. Written in batch B1 after reading each hunk in the Mac copy of 0.1.9 (~/lab/venvs/mhab1012-k314, listing sha256 b38e2cc5..., equal to env/training/hgq2-0.1.9-installed-files.sha256).

0.1.9 wraps every QLayer class build so that check_collapsed_weight evaluates each q<var> property right after build and warns if the quantized weight distribution collapsed (installed base.py:118-140); the snapshot has no wrapper. Consequence (STUDY section 7.3, section 13 binary gates): a binary layer's qkernel must be computable at the end of build
0.1.9 sets a misspelled, never-read attribute _iqs_confs = None; the snapshot drops the line; no effect

the snapshot asserts enable_iq in the iq_confs property; in 0.1.9 the property reads _iq_confs, which is unset when enable_iq is False, and raises AttributeError instead; no effect while enable_iq is True, as in every xfm layer

the snapshot returns early from QLayerBaseMultiInputs.build when enable_iq is False; 0.1.9 goes on, reads iq_confs and fails with AttributeError, so in 0.1.9 a multi-input layer (QAdd and the other merges) cannot be built with enable_iq=False; no effect while enable_iq is True, as in every xfm layer
the snapshot adds the helper _einsum_free0_size, the number of input positions the kernel is applied to
the comment "# not used yet" on the parallelization_factor keyword is dropped (chang review C16 cites it at installed einsum_dense.py:26)
the snapshot sets n_parallel at build and replaces the default factor -1 by n_parallel; 0.1.9 keeps parallelization_factor as passed and never reads it
a comment line is dropped

the snapshot returns ebops * parallelization_factor / n_parallel; 0.1.9 returns ebops (no factor, STUDY section 3.1a). With the default factor the ratio is 1, so the two agree up to the float rounding of x * n / n
the snapshot writes parallelization_factor into get_config; 0.1.9 does not, and gather_vars_to_kwargs keeps it out of the base config, so a 0.1.9 reload uses the default -1
the import of serialize_keras_object, used only by the next hunk
Quantizer.get_config stores the QuantizerConfig object itself in 0.1.9 and serialize_keras_object(config) in the snapshot (quantizer.py:64); the saved form of every quantizer differs

the per-layer EBOPs print runs under "if verbose" in 0.1.9 and "if verbose and record" in the snapshot; with verbose and no EBOPs-enabled layer 0.1.9 raises ValueError (max of an empty sequence); with any EBOPs-enabled layer, as in xfm, both print the same lines
the snapshot imports StopIf into hgq.utils.sugar; 0.1.9 does not, which is why run_train.py:13 needs shim 1
